problemStatement.narrative: Yakko, Wakko and Dot, world-famous animaniacs, decided to rest from acting in cartoons, and take a leave to travel a bit. Yakko dreamt to go to Pennsylvania, his Motherland and the Motherland of his ancestors. Wakko thought about Tasmania, its beaches, sun and sea. Dot chose Transylvania as the most mysterious and unpredictable place. But to their great regret, the leave turned to be very short, so it will be enough to visit one of the three above named places. That's why Yakko, as the cleverest, came up with a truly genius idea: let each of the three roll an ordinary six-sided die, and the one with the highest amount of points will be the winner, and will take the other two to the place of his/her dreams.
problemStatement.task: Yakko thrown a die and got Y points, Wakko — W points. It was Dot's turn. But she didn't hurry. Dot wanted to know for sure what were her chances to visit Transylvania.
conditions: It is known that Yakko and Wakko are true gentlemen, that's why if they have the same amount of points with Dot, they will let Dot win.

inputSpecification.description: The only line of the input file contains two natural numbers Y and W — the results of Yakko's and Wakko's die rolls.

outputSpecification.description: Output the required probability in the form of an irreducible fraction in format «A/B», where A — the numerator, and B — the denominator.

specialCases.condition: The required probability equals to zero

examples.note: Dot will go to Transylvania, if she is lucky to roll 4, 5 or 6 points.

examples.title: Minimum values for both rolls (Y=1, W=1)
examples.why_included: Tests the absolute minimum inputs. Dot wins with any roll (1-6), so the probability is 6/6, which simplifies to 1/1.

examples.title: Symmetric minimum values (Y=1, W=2)
examples.why_included: Tests a case where max(Y, W) = 2. The probability 5/6 is irreducible.

examples.title: Symmetric minimum values (Y=2, W=1)
examples.why_included: Ensures the solution correctly uses max(Y, W) and is not dependent on input order. The result is the same as for '1 2'.

examples.title: Both rolls are equal to 2
